LESSON: THE CELL

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 2.1: The Cell

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on The Cell. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What makes up plant and animal cells?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope
2. describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope
3. compare plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope
4. appreciate the role of cells in living things

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: THE CELL
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
The Cell helps you succeed in INTEGRATED SCIENCE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: THE CELL
Study The Cell like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “The Cell” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why The Cell matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Compare plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope

What this means
In this part you learn to compare plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compare plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to The Cell this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compare plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the role of cells in living things

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of cells in living things. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of cells in living things.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “The Cell” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of cells in living things. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what The Cell is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “The Cell” around your school. (skill: describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope)

Example 2: Say why The Cell matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to The Cell this week. (skill: compare plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “The Cell” around your school. (skill: appreciate the role of cells in living things)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach The Cell to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope.
3. Practise this skill: describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope.
4. Practise this skill: compare plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope.
5. Make one local Kenya example of The Cell from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for The Cell: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study The Cell?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What makes up plant and animal cells?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what The Cell means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope.
5. Be able to: describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
